evidence.quote: Bearer authentication header of the form Bearer
Page index of the results to return. First page is 0.
Last date and time this user logged in.
Whether this user was blocked by an administrator (true) or is not (false).

assumptions: The docs list two auth schemes (bearer token and OAuth2 client credentials) but give no token URL. Only bearer is listed. Auth0 normally issues these tokens from a machine-to-machine app, but that was not in the source. The token needs the read:users scope.

The docs write the host as a tenant-specific domain variable. The host is fixed to the auth0.com vendor domain with the customer's tenant name as the subdomain. Tenants in a region-specific domain (for example your-tenant.us.auth0.com) or using a custom domain may not work with this host; this was not confirmed from the source.

Pagination is page-number based, starting at 0, with a maximum of 100 per page. The source does not say how to tell when the last page is reached, so the runtime is assumed to stop on an empty or short page.

The docs warn this endpoint is not meant for exporting the whole user base. It is eventually consistent, has a ~2 second query limit, and can return 503 on heavy queries. Search-based paging may also be capped on large tenants. The docs recommend a bulk user export for full lists, which is not covered here.
The response is assumed to be a plain array, since include_totals is false by default.
Blocked users are mapped to suspended and all others to active. The source does not describe other states.
User role and user type are not provided by this endpoint, so they are left empty.
last_login is used as the usage signal. It is a per-user field in the user record and may be missing for users who never logged in.
Rate limits were not stated in the source, so they are left empty.
